clue.text: It faces backwards in an old church in ancient city

indicators.note: says the reversed piece sits inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something that faces backwards is turned round, so the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A carving or statue in an ancient church that faces the wrong way, somewhere in an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces backwards' reverses the word It; 'in' then sets the result within the other pieces. 'It' is not a pronoun here but the letters themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a major city of the ancient Greek and Roman world, now Antakya in Turkey.

clue.text: Adult male turned up on peg — Long John Silver?

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: in a down clue a word turned round is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
a tee is the small peg a golfer rests the ball on

explanation.surface: An adult man has been raised up on a wooden peg leg, like the famous pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes UP into PU. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver, the pirate of Treasure Island, has lost a leg, so he is one example of someone with a limb removed.

clue.text: Message online and call from branch?

definitions.meaning: a short post on the social network formerly called Twitter
the chirp of a small bird perched on a branch

explanation.surface: Sending a message on the internet, and a cry heard from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The social-media post took its name from birdsong, so both senses share one word.

clue.text: Offenders at first lie badly, tiddly in court

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word Offenders
tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, so these letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Criminals start telling clumsy lies while tipsy in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'tiddly', British slang for a bit drunk, is what shuffles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Bailey is the popular name of the Central Criminal Court in London.

clue.text: Hotel on Hebridean island raised capital

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: Hotel is the radio alphabet word for H

indicators.note: in a down clue a raised word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A hotel built on a Scottish island has pushed its prices up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IONA into ANOI, which goes beneath H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Our beds damaged unopened flower

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that the flower beds have been spoilt before anything bloomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the letters of OUR BEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebud is a rose before its petals open.

clue.text: One crashes into store — to steal butter?

definitions.meaning: a ... drives a vehicle through a shop front to loot it
read whimsically, one who raids a ram, a ram being an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A criminal smashes into a shop, apparently to make off with some butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but something that butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ram-raiding is the British term for smash-and-grab theft using a car to break the shop window.

clue.text: Bar close to ground reserved

parts.note: save means except or bar, as in all save one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A pub near the football ground has been booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub but means except, which is SAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something saved has been kept back or set aside for later.

clue.text: Clever person after time becomes idiot

indicators.note: the clever person comes after time, below it in this down entry

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing bird
a brain is informal for a very intelligent person

explanation.surface: A bright spark who after a while turns out to be a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD is British rhyming slang (bird-lime, time) for a jail term.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdbrain is an informal word for a stupid, scatterbrained person.

clue.text: Underworld delivered break with church

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the underworld itself
sent means dispatched or delivered

explanation.surface: Hell has delivered a schism from the established church.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent, in Britain, is nonconformity: separation from the established Church of England.

clue.text: Nom de plume that could be Dumpynose?

indicators.note: says the letters of the invented name might be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A writer considers adopting the comic pen name Dumpynose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that could be' signals an anagram of DUMPYNOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nom de plume is a writer's assumed name, a false or pen name.

clue.text: Sport in Six Nations finally showing destructive influence

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

indicators.note: points to the last letter of the word Nations

explanation.surface: Rugby in the Six Nations championship is finally proving a harmful force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Six Nations is the annual European rugby union tournament, which makes 'Sport' fit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is figuratively any corrupting or harmful influence that spreads.

clue.text: Tropical fish in Trent area, oddly

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: Some exotic fish have turned up in the River Trent district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetras are small, brightly coloured freshwater fish from the tropics, popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Non-U Tory following in car unlikely to be caught?

indicators.note: the trimmed Tory comes after the in and the car

parts.note: taken as written
Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: says the letter U is left out of the word

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory is a blue

explanation.surface: A not-very-posh Conservative tailing someone by car hopes not to be spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' (not upper class) drops U from BLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound unlikely to be caught by the ear is one too faint to hear.

clue.text: Poor deal with a sect increased in scale

indicators.note: a poor version of the words is a botched one, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bad bargain struck with a religious group made things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges DEAL + A SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that escalated grew in intensity or size, stepping up by stages.

clue.text: Sound shortened in shout to encourage knight

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the shout

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a sound argument is a valid one

explanation.surface: A noise cut short amid cries urging on a mounted warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is not a noise but valid, as in a sound argument; 'shortened' drops its last letter and 'in' lodges the rest in the shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is French for knight, and was used in English for a member of a knightly order.

clue.text: Champion in great escape

parts.note: top means best or great, as in a top player
flight means fleeing or escape

explanation.surface: A winner caught up in a daring breakout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' is the adjective, as in champion form.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest class, which is what champion means as an adjective.

clue.text: Did spring article in Paris? Fitting!

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written in Paris turned up in springtime, very appropriately.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, to jump or spring.

clue.text: Citrus plant, large, moved one metre

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: A big citrus tree has been shifted one metre over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges ONE METRE after L.
explanation.definitionFit: The lemon tree bears lemons, a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Muscular — like some bully?

definitions.meaning: bully beef is tinned corned beef

explanation.surface: A strongly built thug, like a typical schoolyard tormentor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bully' is not a thug but bully beef, the British name for tinned corned beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy describes someone heavily muscled, and food made of beef.

clue.text: Nightmare with stomach after 10?

indicators.note: the stomach comes after the cross-referenced answer, below it in this down entry

parts.note: the answer to 10 Across is VIRUS, and a bug is a virus
to stomach something is to bear it

explanation.surface: A bad dream about one's belly following an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' points to 10 Across, VIRUS, which is a BUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of dread or annoyance, a figurative nightmare.

clue.text: Extremely pretty country brings burning desire

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A very beautiful land stirs up a passionate longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for pretty but takes its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsive urge to start fires, literally a desire for burning.

clue.text: An unpleasant noise surrounding boy in fairy tale

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed around the boy

parts.note: a is a form of an
a din is a loud unpleasant noise
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A dreadful racket breaks out around a young hero in a children's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps An plus the unpleasant noise around the boy, splitting them so the boy lands between.
explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin is the tale from the Arabian Nights of the boy with a magic lamp.

clue.text: One's achievement in not missing a trick?

definitions.text: One's achievement in not missing a trick?

parts.words: One's achievement in not missing a trick?
parts.note: in bridge, winning every one of the thirteen tricks earns this; the phrase not missing a trick means being alert

explanation.surface: Praise for a sharp-eyed person who never misses an opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'not missing a trick' is taken literally: in bridge, taking every trick in a deal is the top contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam in bridge is winning all thirteen tricks, and generally any clean sweep of a set of titles.

clue.text: Fool across the pond first to decry little book

indicators.note: the first letter of the word decry

parts.note: wee means small or little

explanation.surface: An American idiot is the first to criticise a small volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' means American, from the Atlantic between Britain and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a dull, socially awkward person, a nerd or fool.

clue.text: Liberator freeing fifty as from thick treacle

indicators.note: freeing these letters lets them go from the word

parts.note: molasses is the thick dark syrup also called black treacle
L is fifty in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rescuer releases fifty people, as if pulling them out of syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freeing' takes L and AS out of MOLASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt, freeing them.

clue.text: Hired killer from Daisen, in Japan

indicators.note: says the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: An assassin who came from Daisen, a place in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters straight out of DAISEN IN JAPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert agents in feudal Japan, hired as spies and assassins.

clue.text: North-eastern China's mountainous region

parts.note: NE is the abbreviation for north-east
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and a pal is a mate

explanation.surface: A rugged area in the north-east of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country but rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country containing Everest, so it is a mountainous region.

clue.text: Outcast one left in Devon river

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Exe flows through Devon to the sea at Exmouth
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A castaway has been abandoned beside a river in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone banished from their homeland, an outcast.

clue.text: Ridiculously good parts in snail for instance

indicators.note: the letters are set out absurdly, in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A snail has absurdly fine body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ridiculously' rearranges GOOD PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails and slugs belong to the gastropods, molluscs that move on a muscular foot.

clue.text: Savoury dish, lightly cooked, needs while

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked
a bit is a short while, as in wait a bit

explanation.surface: A savoury meal, only briefly cooked, needs some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rabbit, is melted cheese on toast, a savoury snack.

clue.text: Enter undetected and transgress, bagging duck

indicators.note: to bag is to catch or hold, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to sin is to transgress
the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A poacher sneaks in to break the law, shooting a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal in is to slip into a place quietly without being noticed.
